overview: MPS Budget sessions of the Medford School Committee review and approve annual operating budget proposals, capital requests, and external grant allocations. Spanning from May 2022 through May 2026, the committee conducted public hearings, addressed fixed cost increases, and weighed staffing and academic investments against available municipal revenues. Over successive cycles, the committee submitted municipal requests rising from $72.4 million for FY23 to $87.58 million for FY26. Most recently, the committee approved the preliminary FY27 operating budget, which accommodates a $4.1 million base increase alongside $3.3 million in net reductions. The committee's latest action also instructed district leadership to prioritize restoring a vacant inclusion specialist position as funds become available.

threads.name: Annual municipal operating budget requests
threads.summary: In May 2022, the committee voted to submit an FY23 operating budget request of $72.4 million to municipal government (M03#2). For FY24, the committee approved a municipal request of $71,995,165 following a public hearing on staffing needs and school climate priorities (M04#3). Facing projected deficits in FY25, the committee approved a level-service budget request of $79,399,774 to transmit to the Mayor and City Council (M06#7). Deliberations for FY26 concluded with approval of an $87,583,000 preliminary budget request (M08#3). Most recently, the committee approved preliminary FY27 budget recommendations incorporating a $4.1 million base increase alongside $3.3 million in net reductions (M10#2).

threads.name: ESSER grant allocations and federal funding transitions
threads.summary: During the FY23 budget cycle, the administration established a categorization system to distinguish between recurring operating needs and one-time ESSER grant allocations (M01#2, M01#4). Federal funds were designated for instruments, summer programming, and student transit passes before being integrated into the FY23 presentation (M01#10, M03#1). During FY24 planning, the superintendent adjusted operating allocations to meet budget targets using ESSER grants while the committee discussed the impending funding cliff (M04#1). Grant uncertainties remained a subject of committee review during the FY26 budget approval process (M08#3).

threads.name: Special education and student support staffing
threads.summary: During FY23 budget development, the administration submitted requests for additional adjustment counselors, a career counselor, and high school special education personnel (M01#6, M01#8). In the FY25 budget presentation, proposed reductions affecting guidance and nursing positions prompted extensive public testimony against the cuts (M05#1, M05#2). Middle school guidance staffing levels were evaluated again during FY26 deliberations (M08#3). In the FY27 budget votes, the committee approved the recommended operating plan while explicitly directing that a vacant inclusion specialist position be reinstated when funds permit (M09#1, M10#2).

threads.name: High school facilities, climate, and alternative programming
threads.summary: Early operational reviews identified high school facility needs alongside McGlynn building repairs as capital priorities (M02#5). The committee subsequently incorporated funding into its FY24 budget submission to support recommendations from the Medford High School climate report (M04#2, M04#3). In May 2024, the committee voted to co-locate Curtis-Tufts School with Medford High School in the future building project (M06#3). At the same meeting, the committee approved staffing to pilot an alternative education program for at-risk students following improvements in high school climate survey results (M06#5).

threads.name: Career Technical Education expansion
threads.summary: Chad Fallon presented growing CTE enrollment and equipment acquisitions during FY23 deliberations, requesting two instructor positions and an increase in supply funding (M02#2). In May 2024, the committee voted to request that the school building committee and MSBA explore proposed CTE program expansions and new program offerings within the feasibility study (M06#6).

threads.name: Elementary literacy initiatives and coaching
threads.summary: Suzanne Galusi and Dr. Cushing outlined elementary literacy planning involving Hill for Literacy, DIBELS assessments, and science of reading practices during FY23 budget reviews (M02#4). Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent presented adjustments to the FY24 budget that prompted discussion on elementary literacy coaches (M04#1). The committee subsequently approved an FY24 budget request incorporating funding for four elementary literacy coaches (M04#3).

threads.name: Universal free school meals policy
threads.summary: In May 2022, the committee debated the cost of universal free school lunch after the administration noted financial uncertainty and an estimated $1.5 million expense (M01#11). The committee later approved a motion instructing the district to maintain universal free school meals and to seek supplemental municipal funding if state support did not materialize (M03#2).
